doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Working with Benny Goodman and his drummers
summary: Tommy enjoyed playing with a childhood hero; stories of Goodman's treatment of drummers like Morey Feld.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Did you like working with Goodman? I mean I have to ask you.

I did. It was, you know you had some bizarre moments with him, but you know that was like playing with one of my childhood heroes. He was a giant. And some of the players, you know it was like major league baseball. So I thought it was wonderful. And every once in a while something strange would happen, but the plusses outweighed the minuses.

I think you were safer with Benny in a big band. The more people around, he couldn’t, it was harder to single somebody out. But in Las Vegas, he didn’t like the drummer. who’d been playing with him for years, Morey Feld, who is a perfectly good drummer. And he sent for Mousy Alexander from New York to come all the way to Las Vegas for the last, well, three weeks altogether, Mousy came and played the last two weeks and Morey Feld had to sit there in a tuxedo every night.
He says if you leave you’re not getting paid. So that’s the kind of tricks.
Well Benny was very weird with drummers. I don’t think he liked any drummers after Gene Krupa. And he didn’t like Gene Krupa.
Ed told us a story, maybe he’ll tell you if you ask him about it, how he handled Benny. And it was pretty good. I don’t know if I should go through it now but—
Oh, he made him put the money on the drummer.

Oh, he said he just got — Lionel Hampton said if you have any trouble with Benny, just get weirder than he is. And he did that, and I guess it worked for him at the time. Anyway, everybody’s got Benny stories. So you guys were kind of through the years have been alternating between big bands and combos and some studio work.
